text:
Anna Ramirez: FYI customer AcmeCorp opened a high-severity ticket — they started seeing dramatic p99 spikes (5s -> 18s) and intermittent 429s for generation calls from 09:12 UTC. They pasted traces showing "queueing" in the response and long wait times before workers pick up. Can we triage? cc @Mike Chen @Jordan Lee

Mike Chen: Thanks Anna. Can you paste the route/model + tenant id and an example request? Initial hunch: worker pool saturation / head-of-line blocking from a long-running batch or streaming job.

Anna Ramirez: Tenant: acme_corp (tenant-4021). Route: /v1/generate model: rwd-4-8k. Example they repro with this curl (customer shortened):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4-8k","input":"<~3k token prompt>","stream":true}'
```

Jordan Lee: I'm pulling infra metrics now. On metrics dashboard I'm already seeing per-tenant queue depth for tenant-4021 spike to ~220 at 09:11 UTC and a long tail of in-flight requests >12s. That will block other requests on the same worker pool if we don't isolate. Posting the head log snippet I grabbed: 

```
[09:11:58] worker-12 - queue_depth=211 active_rpcs=8 avg_proc_ms=12000 tenant=tenant-4021
[09:12:05] worker-12 - start_processing req_id=abc123 seq_len=3100 estimated_ms=15000
[09:12:12] router - admit_failure tenant=tenant-4021 reason=queue_full
```

Jordan Lee: Looks like a few long synchronous generation requests are monopolizing slots. Two immediate options: 1) isolate tenant-4021 to a dedicated small pool or 2) enable per-tenant concurrency caps / fair-queueing temporarily. I'm going to check whether a quick route override is possible from Console.

Mike Chen: For short-term mitigation we can also 1) temporally bump pool replicas in us-west2, 2) force-route tenant-4021 to a lower-latency model variant (rwd-4-8k-ll) with faster generation / lower batch sizes, or 3) drop streaming to non-streaming to avoid long-lived streams. I can apply a safe config change to reduce max_batch_size for that pool to 8 which should reduce head-of-line time.

SRE Bot: [automated alert] High queue depth detected -> tenant-4021 on pool inference-usw2. Alert ID: A-202403-7721.

Anna Ramirez: Customer is asking for repro steps they can run — they sent the exact curl above. They're willing to try the fallback route but need clear instructions and a temporary ETA.

Mike Chen: Ok I'm going to apply two quick steps now: scale pool +3 replicas and create a temporary route_override for tenant-4021 to model rwd-4-8k-ll. Commands I'm running: 

```
# scale up pool
redwoodctl scale --pool inference-usw2 --replicas +3 --reason "live triage: tenant-4021 p99 spikes"

# create route override for tenant
redwoodctl route set --tenant tenant-4021 --route /v1/generate --model rwd-4-8k-ll --duration 2h
```

Mike Chen: Also lowering max_batch_size on the pool: 

```
redwoodctl pool-config update inference-usw2 --max_batch_size 8
```

Jordan Lee: I enabled per-tenant queue cap of 50 for tenant-4021 as an emergency limiter to prevent noisy neighbor issues. That will allow the rest of customers on the pool to stabilize. I'm logging the change now.

Sophie Patel: Noted — I'm on the customer call and told them we pushed a temporary route to a lower-latency model and scaled the pool. They saw initial improvement in latency for a subset of requests (p95 dropped to ~800ms) but still seeing some backend 429s for large streaming sessions. Suggested immediate steps for them: 1) set `stream=false`, 2) reduce sequence length if possible, 3) retry with exponential backoff. Sharing sample change: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4-8k-ll","input":"<shorter prompt>","stream":false,"max_tokens":512}'
```

Anna Ramirez: Customer switched to non-streaming and confirmed fewer 429s immediately. They're asking for a root cause and a long-term fix.

Mike Chen: Short term actions (done): scaled pool, route override, reduced batch size, set tenant cap. Next: collect flamegraphs / slow RPC traces for the long-running requests (req_id abc123 + others) and check model kernel saturation. Jordan, can you own triage for next 48h and file a postmortem if we confirm fair-queueing gap?

Jordan Lee: I'll own. Initial hypothesis: lack of per-tenant scheduling + large synchronous generation requests = head-of-line blocking. Longer-term fixes to propose: fair-queueing per tenant, preemption for long-running jobs, or lighter-weight streaming worker path. I'll open an infra ticket and include reproducible tracers and the customer traces.

Sophie Patel: I'll keep customer updated and mark as mitigated for now. Customer wants a timeline for a permanent fix — will push status daily. :thumbsup:

Anna Ramirez: Thanks all. Action items summarized: Jordan -> infra ticket + root-cause, Mike -> follow up on pool config / any kernel optimizations, Sophie -> customer comms and confirm no more 429s. Closing thread for now; reopen if spike recurs. :eyes:
